stage.label: Stage {n} of {total} · {name}
lesson.cross.title: WHITE CROSS
lesson.cross.complete: White cross complete! Tap NEW EXERCISE to repeat it, or move on to lesson 2 · Corners.
lesson.cross.free: Build the white cross with no help: the four white edges around the white center, each one on the face of its color.
lesson.corners.title: WHITE CORNERS
lesson.corners.complete: White layer complete! Tap NEW EXERCISE to keep practicing.
lesson.corners.free: Place the four white corners with no help. The bar at the top tells you when the layer is complete.
msg.broken: The white cross came apart. Tap undo until it's back.
msg.wrong: That turn wasn't it. Tap undo and we'll go on.
msg.cross.take: {piece} is in the white layer but in the wrong place. A half turn of that face sends it down to the {layer} layer.
msg.cross.middle: {piece} is in the middle layer. Bring it to the {layer} layer in 3 turns: the last one puts back whatever the first one moved.
msg.cross.align: {piece} is lit up. Turn the {layer} layer until it sits on the face of the {face} center.
msg.cross.up: {piece} is already on the {face} center's face and white points {dir}. A half turn of that face puts it in place.
msg.cross.flipped: {piece} is on the {face} center's face but flipped: white points sideways. These 4 turns put it in the right way.
msg.corner.align: {piece} is lit up. Turn the {layer} layer until it sits in front of its slot, the one in the pink frame.
msg.corner.take: {piece} is in the white layer but in the wrong place. Take it out in 3 turns and then we place it.
msg.corner.out: {piece} is in front of its slot and white points {dir}. That's 7 turns: the first 4 flip it and the last 3 put it in.
msg.corner.in: {piece} is in front of its slot and white points {dir}. It goes in with 3 turns.
help.title: HELP
help.use.1: Drag a face of the cube to turn that layer.
help.use.2: Drag outside the cube to rotate the whole cube: side to side spins it on itself, up and down tilts it toward you or away. If you flick it, it keeps spinning a little and slows down by itself.
help.use.3: On a phone, use two fingers to rotate the whole cube; twisting your fingers turns it on the screen, like a knob, from any position.
help.use.4: The box in the corner shows the side you can't see.
help.use.5: Below the cube are the icons: undo (back arrow), turns (grid, opens the letters) and scramble (crossed arrows). If the cube is partly solved, scramble asks for confirmation and first solves it by itself so you can see it in order; tap it again to scramble. Press and hold an icon to see its name.
help.use.6: The cube icon, top left, straightens the cube without flipping it: it removes the tilt and brings it face on. Tap it twice in a row (or hold it) to return to the starting position: white on top and green in front.
help.use.7: The 3×3 button next to the title switches to the 2×2 cube and back. Each size keeps its own progress and best time.
help.use.8: Challenge: tap scramble. The clock starts with your first turn and stops when you solve it. The button next to the time pauses it.
help.use.9: Practice: the bar at the top shows which stage of the layer-by-layer method you have reached. There are two lessons: 1 · Cross (the four white edges) and 2 · Corners (it starts with the cross already done). The cube is shown with white on top; the app lights up the piece to move, frames its slot and draws an arrow on the face to turn. When you get it, switch to Piece only or No help.
help.use.10: Your progress is saved in this browser.
not.intro: Each letter turns a face 90° clockwise, looking at it head-on.
not.outro: The letters follow your view: U is always the face you see on top.
